songs.name: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Rochester show with soaring Bird Song & explosive jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The 4/9/82 Community War Memorial concert burns from the opening Alabama Getaway through a blistering first set. Highlights include Jerry’s crystal‑clear lead on Bird Song, a hot China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, and an incendiary Space → The Other One sequence, capped by a heartfelt Brokedown Palace encore. An excellent Miller soundboard capture makes this one of the most listenable 1982 dates.
ai_show_review.review:
What unfolds at Rochester’s Community War Memorial on April 9‑82 is pure, unfiltered Dead fire. From the opening Alabama Getaway the band rides a steady groove that only intensifies, delivering a Bird Song where Jerry’s soaring leads and Brent’s harmonic backing sparkle, while Phil anchors the jam with his trademark rolling bass. The first set peaks with a classic China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition that feels both tight and adventurous. In the second set the band launches into a powerful Space → The Other One stretch, highlighted by a thunderous post‑drums burst that showcases Mickey and Billy’s seamless interplay. To Lay Me Down adds a tender counterpoint before the show closes with a warm, sing‑along Brokedown Palace. Across multiple sources the performance is consistently described as “high energy,” “on fire,” and “explosive,” making this night a standout entry in the early‑‘80s era.

For listeners seeking the clearest window into that evening, Miller’s soundboard (gd1982-04-09.sbd.miller.32716.sbeok.flac16) delivers crisp, clean separation with no dropouts, capturing every nuance from Jerry’s lead lines to Brent’s organ textures. Whether you’re chasing the Bird Song magic or the space‑filled climax of The Other One, this recording offers a balanced, high‑fidelity experience that lets the band’s chemistry shine through.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crisp, clean separation and no audible flaws, providing the most faithful representation of the performance.

key_highlights: Jerry’s crystalline lead work on Bird Song
Hot China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition
Explosive Space → The Other One sequence with strong post‑drums burst
Heartfelt Brokedown Palace encore captured in pristine detail

band_performance.Jerry: Praised for a clean, unprocessed tone and long, soaring lead lines on Bird Song; reviewers cite this as part of his “last great Jerry period.”
band_performance.Phil: Delivers solid, rolling bass throughout; noted for a big intro that powers The Other One, keeping the low end both tight and propulsive.
band_performance.Bob: Vocal mix shines, especially on Bird Song and the ballads; harmonies with Brent are highlighted as strong and well‑blended.
band_performance.Brent: Grainy vocal texture adds character; organ playing described as frenzied and hot‑strutting, with superb harmony backing on New Minglewood Blues and other tunes.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums lock in tightly with Billy, providing a powerful post‑drums sequence that fuels the Space → The Other One explosion.
band_performance.Billy: Provides a steady rhythmic foundation; together with Mickey creates an energetic, cohesive percussion backbone.
